title: Crafting Spend Entry
description: One row of a crafting spend table — an improvement the crafter buys with Advantage/Triumph, or a flaw the GM imposes with Threat/Despair. Shape is concept `crafting-module-concept` §4.4 as AMENDED (Amendment 1, ruling `crafting-spend-cost-shape` Q1 option (a)). THE AMENDMENT IS THE POINT OF THIS FILE: §4.4 originally fixed the price as `cost {symbol, count}` — one symbol, one count — and Jason's completed worksheet falsified it within hours, because 26 of the 29 printed rows price as a CHOICE ('N Advantage OR 1 Triumph'). The implementer halted rather than widening a durable contract under build autonomy (R-Y2-1), and the answer was to adopt the encoding the combat spend tables already ship rather than invent a crafting dialect. PROVENANCE: the OCR of this table rendered its entire cost column as noise; every cost was read from the printed book by Jason, and R-CRAFT-4 makes that worksheet the only legal entry path.

id.description: Stable app-owned row id, unique across BOTH improvements and flaws within a category. Required (the combat spend tables never needed one): once-only enforcement and the GM's recorded flaw picks each reference a specific row, and a crafting session persists those references.

name.description: Display name exactly as printed, e.g. 'Efficient Construction'.

ogg_key.description: OggDude's `CraftImprovement` `Key` for this row (card `release-r5-crafting-sm` ADDENDUM 7, Q1 (a)): the starship rows' field and name, singular because one row stands for one OggDude row (a template's `ogg_keys` is plural because it can fold several). Unique within a category among rows of the same `flags.schematic`, not registry-wide (ruling `release-r5-crafting-up-dupkey` Q1 (a): OggDude doubles `IMPALCHTALDUP` inside one `TempType`, once as Clever Construction and once, with `<Schematic>true`, as the page's Blueprint); the guard is `test/release_r5_crafting_pins.cjs` P4. Written by `scripts/canonical/crafting_sm_batch.py` and `scripts/canonical/crafting_up_batch.py`. Read ONLY by `scripts/canonical/release_r5_accounted.py` (accounting): no import or export path reads it.

exclusive_group.description: Ruling `release-r5-crafting-up-dupkey` Q2 (a) (R-Y2-1): rows sharing a value within a category are ONE printed row that OggDude splits into versions; the value is the printed row's slug (`additional_power`, `empowered`, `mighty`, Unlimited Power p.85). Every member carries the same `flags.once_only`; when it is true, at most one member may be bought per craft (`craftStore.toggleRow` refuses a second). A group whose printed row has no 'once' (Additional Power) is not limited by the group. Whether a member fits a given item is said by its `effects` or `told`, never inferred from its name. Absent = the row is its own printed row.

limits.description: Ruling `release-r5-crafting-kp-c0` Q3b (R-Y2-1): a printed limit on how often, or on what, this row may be bought, other than "(this can only be selected once)" (that is `flags.once_only`). Read by ONE function, craftStore.limitOf(row, base, timesTaken), which eligible, spendLedger, toggleRow, takeAgain and buildItem all call. Sized across every crafting page the programme holds (brief `release-r5-crafting-kp-c0` Q3): one count cap, one refusal. A conditional effect ("If the weapon has …") stays on its effect (`if_present`) or `told`; a value clamp stays on its effect (`cap`/`floor`); a limit on another item stays `told`.

max_count.description: The times this row may be bought on one project: "to a maximum of N" (Extra Hard Point, Keeping the Peace printed 91). `once_only` means 1; the two together are an error.

max_value.description: Ruling `release-r6-companions-c0` Q2 (R-R6CC-2): "to a maximum of N" capping the NUMBER the row moves, not the count (Deflective Carapace, Narrow Profile: "to a maximum of 2", Special Modifications printed 81). Read only by craftStore.limitOf: refused once the base's value plus this row's purchases reach N.

not_for.description: The row is refused when ANY predicate holds on the template's BASE item (its result_profile after its own effects and choice; never the running record, so purchase order cannot change the answer). A CLOSED grammar, grown only by ruling.

field.description: The base item's field read. `tier`: the droid's tier (ruling release-r6-companions-c0 Q2: Adaptive Programming "cannot be applied to minion droids", Special Modifications printed 83); its base is the droid being programmed.

is.description: The value that refuses the row: "cannot be selected for a two-handed lightsaber" (Endless Vigil printed 87) is {field: hands, is: two_handed}.

cost.description: Human-facing price as glyph tokens, same convention as spend_tables.json (e.g. '[AD][AD] or [TR]'). CANONICAL REGISTRY CONTENT, not a persisted projection — the double-brawn guardrail governs character saves, not source data. MUST agree with `req`: the guard derives this string from `req` and compares, so a hand-edit to one that misses the other fails loudly rather than shipping a price the display and the engine disagree about.

req.description: The alternatives that satisfy this row's price. ANY ONE ENTRY PAYS — this is an OR, never an AND. Length 1 is a single-price row (3 of the 29 melee rows: Concussive Quality and Integral Attachment at 2 Triumph, Hidden Flaw at 2 Despair — the ladder deliberately putting them out of Advantage's reach).

items.description: One way to pay: a single symbol key and how many of it. The FIXED vocabulary is ad · tr · th · de (Advantage, Triumph, Threat, Despair), plus ls · ds (light-side and dark-side results), placed on paper by `release-r5-crafting-contract` R-R5CC-4 for the alchemy tables. A row needing any other key is a FRESH R-SY4 HALT, not a quiet addition — the ruling that set this vocabulary applied its own medicine to itself.

ls.description: Light-side result on a Force die (`release-r5-crafting-contract` R-R5CC-4: the alchemy tables price the crafter's rows in light-side results). Improvements only; displayed as [LI]. Spent here, never turned into Force points (Unlimited Power p.80).

ds.description: Dark-side result on a Force die (R-R5CC-4: the GM's alchemy rows). Flaws only; displayed as [DA].

effect.description: What the row does, in this project's own plain mechanical voice — NOT the book's prose (F-EDS-6 is retiring FFG prose from shipped registries). Display text. What the engine APPLIES is `effects` (or nothing, for a `told` row) — `release-r5-crafting-contract` R-R5CC-1 retired the closed code map that used to stand behind this string.

effects.description: R-R5CC-1 (`release-r5-crafting-contract`): what the row does to the crafted ITEM, in the SHARED item grammar — the option effect an attachment line carries (item-common.schema.json base_mods.effect), limited to the ops ItemResolve's option writers apply: quality_add, damage_delta, crit_delta, encumbrance_delta (+ floor), range_delta, defense_delta, soak_delta, hands_set, hard_points_delta, quality_grant; plus qualities_reduce, pool_mod and item_character_effect. lib/shared/crafting.js hands the list to ItemResolve.applyInstalledAttachments as one inline attachment and owns no arithmetic. EXACTLY ONE of effects / vehicle_effects / told on every row (ruling release-r5-crafting-fib-c0 Q2).

droid_effects.description: Ruling `release-r6-companions-c0` Q2 (a) (R-R6CC-2; R-Y2-1): what a DROID row does to the droid it builds or programs, applied at RENDER by the one droid resolver (`droidOf`, lib/shared/companions.js) to the chassis profile. The character grammar's op NAMES with their one meaning each (soak_delta, wound_threshold_delta, defense_delta, characteristic_delta, skill_rank_delta: `charbuild-common` $defs/effect), plus the closed droid ops (silhouette_delta, skill_add, talent_add, talent_rank_delta, cybernetic_add, trait_add). Its own small shape rather than a $ref, because $defs/effect's allOf binds skill_rank_delta to a Force cost, which a droid row never carries. A `target: chosen` op reads the purchase's pick (`picks['<row id>#<n>']`, R-R6CC-5).

vehicle_effects.description: Ruling `release-r5-crafting-fib-c0` Q2 (a) (R-Y2-1): what a FORTIFICATION row does to a vehicle number of the fortification (Forged in Battle printed 85), in the shared vehicle grammar ($defs/vehicle_effect), limited here to passengers_delta (occupancy) and armor_delta (a bunker's armour). Applied by SWRPGVesselResolve.resolve, called by craftStore.fortificationOf with the rows as installed parts in purchase order; an op whose number the fortification does not carry is not applied and is returned in `unapplied` (Q4a (a): "if applicable" is a conditional effect). EXACTLY ONE of effects / vehicle_effects / told on every row; a row needing two is a brief.

reason.description: Why the app does not apply it, in plain words; shown with the row's text and cite.

told.description: R-R5CC-1: a row the shared grammar cannot express — a character write at craft time (strain, Conflict, a Critical Injury), a session or tools effect, or a sheet write (the schematic, ADDENDUM 3). Shown as its text with its cite and remembered (craft_notes), never applied (R-WS-5).

flags.description: All four ship on every row regardless of whether melee uses them (R-CRAFT-2 — retrofitting a flag under live data is the expensive path the rider forecloses). Melee's carriers, now confirmed: 9 once_only, 2 persistent, 0 rolls_subtable.

once_only.description: Printed 'this can only be selected once'. Enforced BY DISPLAY at the surface (concept §4.1), which is why the row needs a stable id.

persistent.description: Outlives the crafting session. Melee's two: Schematic (permanently reduces this template's difficulty for all future builds — the cross-session class the concept cites the droid Program Pattern for) and Hidden Flaw (persists on the weapon until repaired).

rolls_subtable.description: Resolves by rolling on a further table (droid personality is a d100 table). No melee row uses it; droids are last by design.

schematic.description: `release-r5-crafting-contract` ADDENDUM 3: the category's SCHEMATIC row. Buying it on a finished project adds 1 to that template's `sheet.craft_schematics` level (R-R5CC-3); on the item it is `told`. Required on every row like its siblings (R-CRAFT-2); false everywhere but the schematic rows, at most one true per category (test/release_r5_crafting_data.cjs).

extra_copy.description: Ruling `release-r5-crafting-up-extra-copy` Q1 (a) (R-Y2-1): the row's printed text makes one more of the finished thing ('two ... instead of one': Large Batch, Unlimited Power p.82; Clever Construction, p.85). On the item the row is `told`; when a FINISHED project's bought rows include it, the landing arm lands one more `{_inline: record}` of the same record (craftStore.buildItem's copies). A failed check lands nothing. One more, never a count. Required on every row like its siblings (R-CRAFT-2); the true set is pinned by id (test/release_r5_crafting_pins.cjs).

on_failure.description: Ruling `release-r5-crafting-ev-on-failure` Q1 (a) (R-Y2-1): the row's printed symbol cell says '(failed check)' (Learning Experience, Horrible Accident; Endless Vigil Table 3-12, printed 87). Read by the spend (craftStore.affordable): on a FAILED outcome only on_failure rows are affordable; on a successful one they never are. Such a row is `told` and lands nothing (contract ADDENDUM 3: a failed check buys nothing that LANDS). Required on every row like its siblings (R-CRAFT-2); the true set is pinned by id (test/release_r5_crafting_pins.cjs).

cite.description: Page cite in PRINTED numbering (this book's corpus runs +3). Required per row and worksheet-sourced — no cite, no claim.

field.description: The dotted path of the corrected value on this record (e.g. `flags.once_only`).

to.description: The book's value, EQUAL to the record's value at `field`.

cite.description: The printed page that reads it.

why.description: What the page reads, naming the DECISIONS id that read it.

corrections.description: Card `release-r5-board-answers` K2 (R-Y2-1, on paper there): vehicle-weapons' `corrections` item shape, adopted for a crafting row: a value the book prints otherwise than OggDude, held at the book's value. Jason's read of a book board turns an `inferred` entry into one (DECISIONS D-321: Faulty and Ion-Shielded are not once only). No field sits in both `corrections` and `inferred`. Absent = the row holds OggDude's values wherever the page agrees.

field.description: The dotted path of the inferred value on this record (e.g. `req`, `result_profile.crit`).

value.description: The value held, EQUAL to the record's value at `field` (a guard proves it).

cite.description: The printed page whose text lost the value.

inferred.description: `release-r5-crafting-sm-card` ADDENDUM 2 (R-Y2-1), exactly `release-r5-data-card` ADDENDUM 6's shape — one shape, two registries: a value the printed page lost (a cost glyph, a damaged cell), held at OggDude's value until Jason reads the book's board. His read turns an entry into a page correction or removes it. Absent = every value on this record is read off the page.

max.description: a value cap on the moved number (characteristic_delta: 6)

group.description: skill_add: the skills.vocab group the new skill is picked from

how.description: trait_add: chosen by the crafter or GM, rolled on Table 3-11, or the GM's secret
